newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU attempt to control ecstasy and crack.
newsitem.headline: EU attempt to control ecstasy and crack.

text.p: European Union justice ministers vowed on Thursday to curb the manufacture of man-made drugs like ecstasy and crack, increasingly being made within its own borders and on its doorstep in eastern Europe.

As part of the exercise, EU ministers will in November meet colleagues from eastern European countries seen as the source of many of the the popular youth culture tablets, Irish Justice Minister Nora Owen told a news conference during a two-day meeting.

"We are putting man-made drugs on the EU agenda for the first time. Chemical drugs are now flourishing and belong to part of a new youth culture," EU Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin told the conference.
The ministers made limited progress on the tricky issue harmonising drugs legislation within the 15-nation bloc.
Ireland put forward a resolution on uniform sentencing, Owen told the conference, and it will be scrutinised in time for the next ministerial meeting in November with a view to agreement.
"I hope in November we can finalise agreement on this issue such that drug trafficking will be sentenced commensurate with the most serious of crimes," she said.
The EU was reacting to pressure from parents and police because of a spiralling drugs problem in the border-free Union.

Owen said Ireland, the current EU president, already had legislation allowing for life sentences for drugs traffickers and she hoped other member states would treat the traffickers with equal seriousness.

On man-made drugs, Owen said she hoped the EU police force Europol would advance the profiling of such drugs and use chemical analysis find out the country of origin whether it was Poland, Hungary or the Czech Republic or within the EU itself.
EU officials said the move was a recognition that drugs trafficking did not only originate in far away places like Latin America.
Owen said identifying the origin of a drug would be of valuable assistance to those trying to curb trafficking.
The ministers pledged to ratify a convention putting Europol fully into operation before the end of 1997.
Owen said the ministers also discussed relations with the United States, saying coordination with Washington was crucial to the fight against the drugs trade.
